gen-dafont-true-north-fs-rowan: Rowan, a text serif, reads friendly and literary, with generous openings in every curve and thin strokes about half the weight of thick ones. Rowan keeps things gentle, while True North packs a stocky, tall middle band whose curves refuse to close.
gen-dafont-vcr-osd-mono-fs-asap: Asap sets its c as an open arc and lifts its lowercase nearly to the capitals, so lines read quickly. And VCR OSD Mono, made small beside it, would lose its towering fixed-width, code-like presence.
gen-dafont-vcr-osd-mono-fs-epilogue: VCR OSD Mono brings fixed-width, code-style letters with a towering x-height and a lo-fi, retro-tech hum, while Epilogue curves loosely beneath it. Monospace meets sans-serif.
gen-dafont-vcr-osd-mono-fs-fira-sans: Towering lowercase in fixed-width, code-style letters: that is VCR OSD Mono. Fira Sans follows with a larger-than-usual x-height, s curves opening wide at both ends and no thick-thin contrast, so the monospace heading and the sans-serif text feel tidy and related.
gen-dafont-vcr-osd-mono-fs-nunito: VCR OSD Mono looks traced with a single marker tip, every line the same. Nunito answers with big round bowls and terminals that stop well clear of the stem, so it could go a touch larger.
gen-dafont-vcr-osd-mono-general-sans: Lo-fi, retro-tech, and fixed in place: VCR OSD Mono towers with code-style letters. And General Sans fills the line with a steady pen pressure and smooth curves, which makes the sans-serif feel quietly modern next to it.
gen-dafont-verve-fs-epilogue: Verve's thick strokes sit beside hair-thin ones, and its bowls nearly seal shut, which gives big, short headings real bite. Epilogue stays wire-like and curvy underneath, with arches on r, n and m matching their stems.
gen-dafont-verve-fs-hoover: Verve crowds its letters close, with bowls nearly shut and sharp thick-thin strokes. Hoover, a classic serif, gives the eye a generous entry into the e and keeps its ascenders compressed, so a long passage reads sturdy and refined.
gen-dafont-verve-fs-quicksand: Sharp hairlines against heavy strokes, then Verve's tight, nearly closed bowls. And Quicksand, spaghetti-like and uniform, with tall bulb-shaped lowercase, is the one to nudge up in size.
